Title: To Charge or Not to Charge: Autonomous Battery Digital Twin for Electric Vehicles
Source title: IEEE Vehicular Networking Conference, VNC
Affiliations: Indian Institute of Science, Dept. of Electronic Systems Engg., Benguluru, India
Authors with affiliations: Poola L., Indian Institute of Science, Dept. of Electronic Systems Engg., Benguluru, India; Hasabnis K.R., Indian Institute of Science, Dept. of Electronic Systems Engg., Benguluru, India; Prabhakar T.V., Indian Institute of Science, Dept. of Electronic Systems Engg., Benguluru, India
Abstract: Although environmental awareness is accelerating towards green transport, electric vehicle (EV) adoption is hindered due to range anxiety. Range anxiety is the fear of a dead battery before reaching the destination or the next charging station. This can be addressed by accurate state-of-charge (SoC) estimation combined with an optimal policy guarantees reaching the destination. In this work, we propose an integrated model that combines a battery digital twin (DT) to predict battery SoC with the Markov decision process (MDP) as the decision engine. Real-time sensor data from the physical battery running on the drive cycles (CLTC and UDDS) is collected and stored in the cloud to enable remote access and processing. The DT is built based on the physics-based 2RC battery model combined with an extended Kalman filter (EKF) to estimate SoC. The MDP formulates optimal actions based on the DT SoC predictions and the route. The dynamic closed-loop integration between DT and MDP is robust and can adapt to different drive cycle transitions while considering battery SoC & Temperature uncertainties, mimicking real-life scenarios to address range anxiety. The DT's prediction accuracy is validated by comparing the estimated and measured SoC, and the experimental results show the prediction error remains below 0.3%. MDP's decision strategy is validated through a case study. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: This paper presents a deep learning-based octagonal moiré alignment method that enables wafer-to-wafer bonding with submicron accuracy for an ultrathin device stacking platform. The approach uses concentric octagonal moiré gratings embedded in the metal layer and leverages near-field contrast inversion to achieve robust infrared alignment. To address limited labeled experimental data, we built a digital-twin training pipeline that combines physics-based synthetic moiré generation with real infrared images. After accounting for label uncertainty from the vernier-based metrology, the model reached an estimated real image precision on the order of tens of nanometers and predicts in-plane translation and rotation using a single mark. The method was validated by fabricating a three-layer active device stack with maintained interlayer alignment on the order of a few hundred nanometers, demonstrating a practical path toward high-density three-dimensional integration. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is a foundational capability for operating power systems with high shares of variable renewable generation. However, the methodological landscape is fragmented across physical-based models, statistical time-series approaches, machine learning (ML), and increasingly diverse hybrid and multi-modal pipelines combining SCADA measurements with numerical weather prediction (NWP) and remote-sensing data. This paper provides a unified, practice-oriented synthesis of PV power forecasting methods, linking forecasting tasks and horizons to data requirements, modeling assumptions, and deployment constraints. We first summarize PV plant architecture, the energy conversion chain and key definitional choices (AC vs. DC, power vs. energy, spatial aggregation, sampling interval). We then formulate the forecasting problem across point and probabilistic settings, distinguishing single- and multi-step strategies and showing how horizon choice shifts the balance between persistence, cloud-driven dynamics, and NWP-driven uncertainty. We propose a taxonomy covering (i) physics-based approaches (clear-sky and PV performance models), (ii) statistical and time-series baselines, (iii) ML/DL families — recurrent, convolutional, attention-based, and transformer architectures — and (iv) hybrid and ensemble methods, with attention to calibration and uncertainty quantification. Finally, we identify open challenges limiting robust deployment — non-stationarity, cross-site/climate generalization, probabilistic calibration, and explainability — and highlight emerging trends such as self-supervised learning, foundation models, and digital-twin-inspired forecasting loops. © 2026 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.

Title: A Hierarchical Business Model for Translating Digital Twins: A Case Study for Health Care Applications From Research to Market

Abstract: Digital twins (DTs) are rapidly emerging as a transformative technology in health care, offering real-time, data-driven simulations of organs, patients, and hospital systems. These virtual models enhance the accuracy of predictive diagnostics, the effectiveness of personalized therapies, and operational efficiencies; thus, making them a strategic asset for both clinical care and business considerations. While these technologies originated in aerospace and manufacturing, health care applications of DT are accelerating significantly, primarily driven by advances in artificial intelligence (AI), cloud computing, and wearable sensors (e.g., IoT: Internet of Things). The global market for DT in health care applications is projected to grow from $2.7 billion in 2024 to nearly $60 billion by 2030, signaling a shift in how health care is delivered, funded, and optimized. This study is focused on developing a structured four-stage framework for translating DT innovation into scalable clinical solutions, from early-stage research and pilot programs to commercialization and full-scale hospital integration. The authors compared platforms established by enterprises with those developed by startups. By exploring a case study of a DT for cardiovascular applications, the role of targeted value propositions, regulatory alignment, and staged funding strategies is illustrated. Key enablers such as “software as a medical device pathway,” AI, and interoperability standards (e.g., for IoT) are discussed alongside business model design and stakeholder alignment. The results of this case study can provide a practical roadmap for entrepreneurs, investors, and corporate leaders in the health care sector. This case study can provide a pathway for professionals aiming to capitalize on the convergence of digital health, personalized medicine, and value-based care. These topics related to DT are to fostering innovative organizational strategies and essential for addressing business imperatives that are redefining competitive advantages. Abstract: Uncertainties and disruptions across value chains, from supply chains to shopfloor resources, significantly impact production systems. Addressing these challenges requires manufacturing systems that are both resilient and reconfigurable to maintain robust and flexible operations. This work presents a conceptual framework to improve the resilience and reconfiguration capabilities of manufacturing systems at the machine level. The resilience quantification and reconfiguration support are enabled by dataspaces and the Asset Administration Shell (AAS). The goal is to facilitate shopfloor workers in measuring resilience and implementing reconfiguration strategies effectively in response to disruptions. This framework is designed with the focus on progressive forming press machines potentially supporting digital manufacturing. The findings reveal the possibility for production systems to be adaptable and robust. Future work will focus on implementation and evaluation of the proposed framework and scaling it to other manufacturing processes. © The Author(s) 2026.

Abstract: As digital twins (DTs) become foundational technologies for critical infrastructure (CI), their integration with artificial intelligence (AI) creates new opportunities and risks for financial security, financial intelligence, and governance resilience. Beyond technical and cybersecurity threats, human factors - including decision-making biases, operator trust, and organisational behaviour - significantly influence cyber-financial exposure and the economic performance of DT ecosystems. This paper proposes a human-centric and AI-augmented financial risk management (FRM) framework for secure DTs in CI. The approach integrates real-time DT data, AI-based predictive analytics, explainable decision support, and human-in-the-loop (HITL) mechanisms. It comprises four interconnected components: (1) AI-based forecasting of operational failures and financial losses; (2) behavioural modelling of decision-makers under uncertainty; (3) trust-aware and explainable AI (XAI) mechanisms; and (4) dynamic allocation of financial resources according to risk exposure and infrastructure state. Its methodological contribution is a hybrid decision architecture that links technical system conditions with financial decision-making through a trust-weighted optimisation function, formalised alongside an aggregate financial risk index (FRI) and a Markowitz-style cybersecurity-budget allocation. The framework is assessed through scenario-based simulation for energy and smart-city infrastructure, with parameters informed by open-source cybersecurity and risk-management materials (ENISA threat-landscape reports, NIST IR 8286 Rev. 1, IBM/Ponemon Cost of a Data Breach Report 2025). For the illustrative configuration considered, total expected financial losses across five representative disruption scenarios decrease from 5.82 to 2.70 million USD - a reduction of 53.6% - relative to a baseline FRM without HITL/XAI integration. The results indicate that integrating human expertise, explainable AI, and secure DT technologies can improve financial resilience, reduce disruption costs, and increase trust in AI-supported infrastructure governance. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: Stereovision can be defined as a measurement process reliant on multiple images taken from different perspectives to estimate three-dimensional dense informations and parameters, thereby enabling the metrological evaluation of form errors and surface texture parameters. Digital Metrological Twin is defined as a numerical model that depicts a specific measurement process and indicates an associated measurement uncertainty for a specific measurement value, which is traceable to the units of the international system of units. A comprehensive literature review on the integration of stereovision systems and digital metrological twins has been conducted using a PRISMA methodology, exploring different applications, frameworks and challenges. Digital twins of stereovision systems could be useful tools for developing, modeling, testing, and optimizing the usage of stereovision in many industrial contexts. By bridging the gap between the digital and physical domains, they enable virtual testing and validation and pave the way for the more accurate, effective and efficient implementation of stereovision technologies in the real world. This review reveals a major barrier to the integration of digital twins and stereovision systems for industrial applications in terms of availability of standards among hardware, software, and data layers. Achieving high accuracy in intelligent industrial settings is limited due to increased complexity, expenses and lack of calibration standards for stereovision systems. Future efforts to resolve these gaps will aid in promoting widespread adoption. This research is beneficial for the creation of a digital twin for a stereovision 3D scanning system being developed at LNE in the scope of the 23IND08 Di-Vision project. © 2026 EUSPEN. Abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) geological modeling is a modern way to characterize subsurface conditions and support underground digital twins. An essential task is to effectively utilize all available site investigation data and quantify geological uncertainty. This paper presents a generic 3D probabilistic geological modeling framework to fuse multisource data and quantify and reduce geological uncertainty. Data from geophysical tests, boreholes, standard penetration tests (SPTs) and cone penetration tests (CPTs) are integrated utilizing Bayesian sequential updating and density-corrected k-nearest neighbors (kNN) interpolation techniques. Compared with standard kNN, the density correction mitigates bias from clustered data. This framework was applied to two large areas in Hong Kong, and demonstrated more-robust performance and higher computational efficiency than traditional methods. Step-by-step integration of different data sources improves model accuracy and reduces uncertainty, with borehole data contributing the most, followed by CPT and then SPT. In areas with limited borehole data but sufficient geophysical, SPT, or CPT data, the method still can accurately identify geological types. The resulting geological model enables reliable spatial-temporal settlement prediction considering geotechnical and geological uncertainties. The framework enhances the accuracy of 3D geological modeling for large-scale sparse data sites and supports interactive model updates when new data become available.  © 2025 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: PerioTwin-DeltaCRED: a validation-aware physiological digital twin for longitudinal periodontal treatment response prediction
Source title: Frontiers in Physiology
Affiliations: Department of Periodontics, Saveetha Dental College and Hospitals, Saveetha Institute of Medical and Technical Sciences (SIMATS), Chennai, India
Authors with affiliations: Yadalam P.K., Department of Periodontics, Saveetha Dental College and Hospitals, Saveetha Institute of Medical and Technical Sciences (SIMATS), Chennai, India
Abstract: Background – Predicting individual periodontal treatment response remains clinically unresolved. Existing machine-learning models are predominantly cross-sectional, lack a longitudinal response-vector design, and are rarely evaluated within validation-aware digital-twin frameworks that capture multidimensional credibility rather than single-endpoint discrimination alone. This study aimed to develop and evaluate PerioTwin-DeltaCRED, a validation-aware periodontal digital twin that models treatment response as a longitudinal PPD and CAL response vector, and to benchmark classical and quantum machine-learning engines against that framework. Methods – Five hundred patients with Stage II-IV periodontitis were retrospectively assembled from the Saveetha DIAS system; treatment was observational, involving either scaling and root planing alone or with low-level laser therapy. A stratified 60:20:20 split (training n=300, validation n=100, test n=100) was used for all models, using only baseline predictors—follow-up measurements and outcome variables were excluded to prevent leakage. Classical learners (logistic regression, random forest, gradient boosting) were benchmarked for poor-response classification, PPD reduction, CAL gain, and residual deep-pocket risk. Three quantum architectures—VQC-Pauli, Data Re-Uploading VQC (DRU-VQC), and QSVC—along with a hybrid quantum–classical stack, were evaluated as exploratory engines; six principal components (83.6% of variance) were angle-encoded into six-qubit circuits. Hyperparameters were optimized by Optuna on the validation set, with the test set withheld until final assessment. Uncertainty was estimated by bootstrap resampling, and the Delta-PTFI summarized credibility. Results – Classical logistic regression was the strongest poor-response model (test AUROC 0.69, 95% CI 0.59–0.80; sensitivity 0.54, specificity 0.75), with random forest comparable (AUROC 0.68) and providing the best residual deep-pocket discrimination (AUROC 0.76). Continuous responses were predicted with modest error (PPD-reduction mean absolute error 0.37 mm; CAL-gain 0.31 mm); against observed changes of 1.20 ± 0.46 mm and 0.78 ± 0.36 mm, these errors were equivalent to an intercept-only baseline. Baseline CAL and periodontal stage were the dominant and most stable predictors (mean top-5 stability 0.75), and a two-variable model using stage and baseline CAL alone matched the full model (AUROC 0.71 versus 0.69). An exploratory composite credibility index (Delta-PTFI) was 0.62, falling to 0.25 when its continuous-outcome components were anchored to an intercept-only reference. No quantum architecture surpassed classical learning: the data re-uploading classifier (DRU-VQC) was the best quantum model (test AUROC 0.63), followed by the hybrid stack (0.60), VQC-Pauli (0.46), and QSVC (0.40). Classical learners restricted to the same six principal components reached AUROC 0.58–0.66, and the best of them (random forest, 0.66) still exceeded every quantum model. Conclusion – PerioTwin-DeltaCRED provides a validation-aware digital twin for periodontal treatment response, assessing calibration, fidelity, response stability, and credibility index instead of just discrimination. Classical models outperformed, and quantum architectures like DRU-VQC showed no advantage in noiseless six-qubit tests. This is among the first studies embedding and benchmarking quantum machine learning in a periodontal digital twin; more validation and noise testing is needed before clinical use. Title: Models and modeling in human geography I: Classic or new, uncertainty and tradeoffs remain
Source title: Progress in Human Geography
Affiliations: Center for Geospatial Sciences, School of Public Policy, University of California at Riverside, Riverside, CA, United States
Authors with affiliations: Grubesic T.H., Center for Geospatial Sciences, School of Public Policy, University of California at Riverside, Riverside, CA, United States
Abstract: Human geographers are constantly endeavoring to deepen our understanding of patterns and processes. As a result, we have no shortage of models to simplify, visualize, explain, and predict human activity on Earth. However, recent advances in geographic modeling approaches are rapidly changing how we address contemporary geographic problems. In this first progress report, I provide an overview and typology of uncertainty in human geography models, enabling researchers to make more informed decisions about their data pipelines and modeling choices. In particular, this work explores uncertainty in classic, deductive models, inductive models, agent-based models, and spatial digital twins. © The Author(s) 2026. Title: Digital Twin for Context Awareness, Security, and Resilience in Vehicular Networks for 5G and Beyond: A Comprehensive Survey
Source title: IEEE Open Journal of the Communications Society

Abstract: Effective vehicular network management is essential for enabling reliable communications between vehicles and infrastructure in dynamic environments. The integration of terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks (NTNs), together with the growing adoption of the Internet of Things (IoT) and diverse vehicular applications, introduces multifaceted challenges in context awareness, security, spectral resource management, and network resilience. Digital twin (DT) technology offers a promising paradigm for addressing these challenges by providing high-fidelity virtual representations of physical network entities that enable predictive simulation, what-if analysis, and proactive closed-loop control. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of DT-enabled vehicular network management. First, the bidirectional relationship between artificial intelligence (AI) and DT is explored, in which AI serves as a key enabler of DT-assisted operations by supporting intelligent sensing, state prediction, anomaly detection, and adaptive decision-making, while DT environments facilitate safe and efficient AI training and validation. Subsequently, a novel DT-driven functional taxonomy is proposed, organizing the literature by DT functionality layers (sensing, prediction, control, feedback, resilience and security), with NTNs and terrestrial networks serving as cross-layer enablers. Based on the identified research gaps, an NTN-integrated, context-aware, and multi-function DT framework is presented to support proactive, resilient, and intelligent vehicular network management for 6G and beyond. The framework addresses critical operational requirements, including DT state modeling and prediction, DT synchronization in dynamic environments, and integrated multilevel data management and computing. Two illustrative case studies are discussed, focusing on DT-assisted radio resource management under channel-modeling uncertainty and DT synchronization under constrained communication resources. Finally, open research challenges and future directions are outlined toward scalable, interoperable, and trustworthy DTs for vehicular networks. © 2020 IEEE.

Abstract: Background – Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection remains a global health challenge, necessitating personalized treatment strategies to optimize patient outcomes. Digital twin technology—synchronized with real-world entities—offers a pathway to precision medicine in HIV care. Methods – We analyzed 5, 436 HIV patients (2016–2024) with demographic, immunologic, and antiretroviral therapy (ART) information. Core algorithms comprised gradient boosting and random forest ensembles; deep architectures (LSTM and Transformer networks) were evaluated as comparative benchmarks on longitudinal feature tensors under identical supervision. Models used five-fold cross-validation, regularization, dropout, and early stopping. A probabilistic treatment ranking layer generated diversified regimen suggestions conditioned on model outputs. Results – Ensemble models achieved strong explained variance on the registry-defined CD4 label (test R2 up to 0.97; cross-validation stability reported in the Results). Deep models achieved comparable held-out accuracy on the same endpoint; the ranking module produced balanced regimen distributions in an illustrative optimization cohort. Simulated digital twin scenarios demonstrated counterfactual CD4 projections under alternative ART strategies for low, moderate, and higher baseline immunology profiles. Discussion – The specific contribution is an explicit patient-state → prediction → regimen exploration pipeline suited to integration with telehealth analytics (risk dashboards, adherence supports), while transparently acknowledging endpoint and leakage limitations and the need for prospective outcome validation. A pragmatic HIV treatment optimization strategy is to route model-supported prioritization into clinician-facing dashboards and remote monitoring workflows rather than autonomous prescribing. Abstract: Several of the next generation nuclear reactors being considered will require autonomous maintenance capabilities, due to the hostile radiation and thermal environments that exclude human operators from supporting equipment in close proximity to the reactors. Research is ongoing to use virtual training environments to train robots to perform maintenance and emergency response operations. Since future designs are still under development, there is no testbed for physical experiments. To overcome this obstacle, we have developed a generalized methodology to train robots in a virtual environment. In this regard, the virtual environment can be created from either 3-D mapping of existing physical components or from components that only exist as engineering specifications, as long as their dimensions and behaviors can be represented in the virtual world. Our approach creates an integrated software and algorithm architecture with the ability to “teach” automated systems successful tasks from simulated data sets with minimal human oversight. In this work, we develop a digital-twin system for training and real-time control of a robotic arm. The digital twin comprises a virtual training environment and a real-time control interface. The virtual training environment allows simulation of maintenance tasks under diverse domain randomizations. After training, the physical robot is controlled while monitoring anticipated behavior of the digital twin in real time. This approach increases operator confidence and can decrease risk compared to deployment of a model without real-time supervision of the digital-twin alongside the physical machine. It is clear that this approach has extensive applications to terrestrial and space-based tasks. Autonomous systems including robots, will support future maintenance and security protocols and this method provides one possible approach to address future uncertainties or responses to accidents. This technology is in its infancy but expected to mature rapidly and undertake complex and dynamic tasks using reinforcement learning derived algorithms. © 2025 American Nuclear Society.

Abstract: Visual navigation offers a low-cost, information-rich solution for agricultural robots, but its deployment is constrained by the diversity and uncertainty of agricultural environments. This review systematically evaluates key technologies—path extraction, tracking control, and multisensor integration—through the S2TAP framework, which examines five interconnected dimensions: Scenario structure, sensing modality, task abstraction, agent mobility, and performance trilemma (the inherent difficulty of simultaneously maximizing accuracy, efficiency, and robustness). The analysis reveals a fundamental dichotomy between wheeled agents (precision tracking) and tracked agents (disturbance rejection), and identifies deep learning’s accuracy gains at the cost of efficiency. Based on these trade-offs, the paper proposes actionable pathways including geometry-first perception, hardware-aware neural architecture search (HW-NAS), uncertainty-aware control, and community-driven standardization (AgriROS and digital twins). Emerging frontiers such as neuromorphic vision and federated learning are also discussed, providing a road map toward robust, scalable visual navigation for autonomous agriculture. This paper presents a structured narrative review that synthesizes the literature through a novel analytical framework rather than an exhaustive systematic review. The paper provides a good reference for the development of visual navigation technology for agricultural robots and vehicles. Copyright © 2026 Yu Han and Zhiyu Song. Title: Introduction
Source title: Technological Advancements and Artificial Intelligence Innovations
Abstract: This book examines the accelerating convergence of advanced computation, data-intensive engineering, and artificial intelligence as a foundational driver of scientific discovery and industrial transformation. It surveys contemporary AI paradigms; supervised, unsupervised, and self-supervised learning; deep neural architectures for perception and representation; foundation models; and emerging agentic and tool-augmented systems, and situates them alongside enabling technologies such as ubiquitous sensing, edge-to-cloud computing, digital twins, high-throughput experimentation, autonomous laboratories, and nanoscale characterization. Across multidisciplinary case studies spanning energy systems, geoscience, materials and chemical engineering, agriculture, and public health, the volume highlights how modern AI pipelines are architected end-to-end: problem formulation, data acquisition and governance, feature/representation learning, model training, evaluation, and deployment into decision workflows. Emphasis is placed on validation in complex, real-world environments, including uncertainty quantification, robustness to distribution shift, interpretability and explainability, and human-in-the-loop design for high-stakes settings. The book also addresses practical implementation constraints that frequently determine success in applied AI: data quality and provenance, class imbalance, label scarcity, privacy and security considerations, scalability across heterogeneous compute and instrument platforms, interoperability with legacy engineering tools, and lifecycle maintenance through monitoring and continuous improvement. Ethical and responsible adoption is treated as a technical requirement, with attention to transparency, auditability, reproducibility, and risk-aware governance. By integrating methodological foundations with implementation patterns and domain exemplars, the text provides readers with a cohesive technical roadmap to current innovations, such as physics-informed learning, multimodal fusion, and digital-twin-driven optimization, and to emerging research directions shaping the next generation of intelligent systems. © 2027 Daniel Asante Otchere.

Abstract: Transitioning to low-carbon energy systems has significantly increased the operational and interconnection complexities of sustainable energy technologies across the power, heat, fuel, and mobility sectors. The high penetration of variable renewable energy sources (VRES), combined with electrification and sector coupling, requires advanced frameworks to manage uncertainty, nonlinearity, and system-level interactions. The emergence of digital intelligence, including artificial intelligence (AI), digital twins, data-driven analytics, and cyber-physical control (CPC), has improved the performance and resilience of modern energy systems. This comprehensive review endeavours to furnish a critical synthesis that encapsulates and evaluates the recent advancements and innovations that have emerged within the realm of digital intelligence, particularly as it is applied to various sectors, including renewable power generation, hydrogen and electrochemical systems, energy storage technologies, and the design and operation of smart buildings, as well as the intricate dynamics associated with integrated multi-energy infrastructures. Special emphasis will be given to system architectures, hybrid physics/data modelling approaches, real-time optimisation strategies, and quantitatively reported improvements in efficiency, emissions mitigation, and operational cost reduction. Additionally, techno-economic and life cycle considerations will be examined to assess sustainability impacts. Finally, technical, organisational, and regulatory challenges will be identified, and future research directions will be outlined to support scalable and reliable digitalised energy systems, thereby contributing to SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG 13 (Climate Action). © 2026 The Author(s). Abstract: The integration of grid-connected solar and wind energy systems introduces variability and uncertainty that challenge conventional power system simulation approaches. While detailed electrical and control models are widely available, environmental factors governing renewable resource availability are often simplified or treated as spatially uniform. This paper presents a grid-connected co-simulation framework that integrates Unreal Engine 5 (UE5) and MATLAB/Simulink to model renewable energy generation under environment-dependent conditions. UE5 simulates solar photovoltaic and wind power generation based on realistic environmental geometry, including sun position, shading, terrain, and obstacle effects. Simulink integrates the generated power with electrical load models and grid interface components, enabling analysis of the net power exchanged with the grid. Solar PV output is driven by daily sun rotation and scene-based occlusion, while wind energy accounts for obstacle-induced attenuation using a Niagara-based flow representation. A case study demonstrates that this framework effectively captures site-specific ramping events and power fluctuations induced by physical surroundings, providing a high-fidelity tool for microgrid stability analysis and the development of Digital Twins for complex power system environments. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: This paper uses a bibliometric approach to map the literature on harnessing Digital Twinning concepts, models, and applications in the context of material and structural fatigue. It aims to explore how this topic has developed over time, identify key researchers contributing significantly to the field, and analyze the network connections among researchers in this rapidly growing area of structural mechanics. Additionally, a frequency-based co-occurrence study was conducted to find the most relevant keywords in scientific publications related to Digital Twins in mechanical fatigue. Several keywords were selected as control terms to create a conceptual thematic map, which visualizes the main research trends. The findings reveal broad interdisciplinary effects across various engineering fields by highlighting three interconnected themes: Digital Twinning for uncertainty quantification and optimization, Finite Element Analysis for fatigue life-based design and simulation, and Structural Health Monitoring for damage detection in materials and structures. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

Title: An adaptive digital twin framework for flow shop scheduling and production planning with machine learning integration
Source title: International Journal of Production Research
Affiliations: School of Industrial Engineering, College of Engineering, University of Tehran, Tehran, Iran; Research Center of Performance and Productivity Analysis, Istinye University, Istanbul, Turkey; Department of Industrial Engineering, Hainan Bielefeld University of Applied Sciences, Hainan, China
Authors with affiliations: Ziari M., School of Industrial Engineering, College of Engineering, University of Tehran, Tehran, Iran; Ghomi-Avili M., School of Industrial Engineering, College of Engineering, University of Tehran, Tehran, Iran; Tavakkoli-Moghaddam R., School of Industrial Engineering, College of Engineering, University of Tehran, Tehran, Iran, Research Center of Performance and Productivity Analysis, Istinye University, Istanbul, Turkey; Foumani M., Department of Industrial Engineering, Hainan Bielefeld University of Applied Sciences, Hainan, China
Abstract: Demand fluctuations, machine downtime, and execution plans’ uncertainties affect production planning and scheduling in flow shops; therefore, these factors must be considered during planning to prevent operational disruptions. Unlike existing static integrated planning and scheduling models or heuristic-based dynamic approaches, this work introduces a closed-loop Digital Twin (DT) framework that preserves the mathematical optimality of a Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Programming (MINLP) model while enabling real-time adaptability. Our primary innovation is the systematic and real-time integration of Support Vector Machine (SVM)-based demand forecasting and Association Rule Mining (ARM)-based proactive downtime prediction. We develop a data-driven DT that synchronises the MINLP with live shop-floor data. The framework integrates SVM for demand forecasting and ARM for proactive machine downtime prediction. Through event-driven re-optimisation, the DT continuously updates key parameters and triggers schedule revisions in response to operational deviations. Computational experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach reduces total operational costs by 13%, significantly decreases machine waiting times and unscheduled downtime, and improves schedule stability compared to static and data-driven baselines. The results underscore the unique value of closed-loop adaptive systems in enhancing resilience and efficiency. This study bridges the gap between traditional optimisation models and real-world execution to offer more responsive and robust production systems. © 2026 Informa UK Limited, trading as Taylor & Francis Group.

Abstract: Digital twins represent virtual replicas of real-world production systems, providing a foundation for data-driven process analysis and optimisation. A key application of digital twins is supporting life cycle assessments (LCA), which evaluate the environmental impacts of products and processes. Traditionally, LCA have relied on literature-based or estimated data, which are often outdated, incomplete, and difficult to verify. These static data sources cannot reflect dynamic changes in production and therefore limit the precision and relevance of environmental assessments. In contrast, continuous, sensor-based time series data generated directly on the shop floor offer a significantly higher level of accuracy, traceability, and timeliness. They capture actual process conditions with standardised measurement methods and quantifiable measurement uncertainty, enabling LCA to reflect real-time, site-specific environmental performance. This opens the opportunity to improve the transparency, precision, and continuous updateability of environmental assessments within digital twins. However, existing methods for assessing data uncertainty, such as the pedigree matrix, were designed for literature- or estimate-based data and fail to capture the specific quality features of time series data. Classical pedigree dimensions, such as source credibility or estimation character, are inadequate for empirically measured, traceable data. This paper therefore aims to adapt selected dimensions of the pedigree matrix to account for the characteristics of time series data, and to develop an uncertainty score based on these adaptations. This score will allow the information-technical uncertainty of continuous production data to be systematically and transparently quantified. By formally linking data quality to LCA model validity, companies can make more informed decisions on which data to use for robust, up-to-date, and dynamic sustainability assessments in the context of digital twins. Abstract: The Dynamic Data Driven Applications Systems (DDDAS) paradigm has endured since its inception in 1980, and starting in 2000, science and technology (S&T) developments have exploited the key tenet of DDDAS of combining executing models with instrumentation data estimation as well as augmented data from other models. More recently, similar paradigms have been adopted by the artificial intelligence (AI) community such as generative adversarial networks (GANs), with the difference being that, in GANs, the seeded augmented data comes from a corpus of represented data versus DDDAS, wherein data augmentation results from first-principle physical modeling. In the preceding DDDAS handbooks, various theoretical and strategic approaches were shown that integrate augmented data from models with that of real-time data or targeted data from archival collections. This introductory chapter highlights recent advances by the DDDAS community such as physics-enhanced machine learning (PEML), uncertainty-aware digital engineering, and edge computing. Each of these methods utilizes the DDDAS paradigm, such as PEML applying the traditional DDDAS methods with a high-fidelity systems model orchestrated with an instrumented system. Digital engineering with “dynamic” digital twins (DTs) utilizes the advances in the past decade to process large amounts of data to provide augmented data for analysis. As from the first handbook, edge computing includes instrumentation systems to control the uncertainty by incorporating computed knowledge to maintain a system’s function when real-time data is incomplete. This introductory chapter highlights some of the broader scopes of the science and technology developments under the rubric of DDDAS as well as the DDDAS impact over time in challenging application areas and in emerging directions of artificial intelligence, digital twins, edge computing, communication networks, and related advances based on the DDDAS paradigm tenets. Additional information and archival materials are available in the DDDAS society’s website: www.1dddas.org. © InfoSymbiotic Systems Society 2026.

Title: A robust offline digital twin for regenerative wastewater treatment: Multi-pollutant stress testing and resilience analysis

Abstract: The challenge that faces municipal wastewater treatment plants as of today is the extreme variability in hydraulic loads and contaminant inflow caused by the constant climatic changes, aggressive urbanization, as well as outdated infrastructure. The traditional measures of performance that only measure mean effluent concentrations cannot capture the regulatory shortcomings that present themselves in transient moments of stress. In response to this shortcoming, this paper suggested a powerful offline digital-twin model that regeneratively works on wastewater treatment, with machine-learning-comprising effluent prediction and multi-pollutant stress testing, with increased resilience indicators, and sensitivity analysis of nature-based solutions (NBS). The random-forest regressors were used to predict the suspended solids (SS), Biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) and the chemical oxygen demand (COD) using large volumes of operational data. The digital twin demonstrated good predictive performance of the biochemical parameters; although the projection of SS had a relatively lower fidelity because of the stochastic nature of hydraulic shear and settling. The regulatory stress test introduced a good foundation of vulnerability particularly manifested in regard to BOD. Efficiency-based NBS attenuation envelope simulated regenerative conditions to formulate the greatest attainable treatment potential. According to the results, restorative interventions are efficient in suppressing regulatory violations in relation to SS and BOD and in guaranteeing a high level of compliance among COD through moderate efficiency ranges. The sensitivity analysis indicated the non-linear resilience returns, with saturation levels attained and decreasing marginal returns to pollution reduction due to pollutant-specific returns to efficiency. In turn, the suggested framework provides a transferable decision support system that focuses on resilience-oriented planning of regenerative wastewater systems that will be able to serve effectively in uncertainty conditions. © (2026), (Polskie Towarzystwo Inzynierii Ekologicznej (PTIE)). Title: A generalized concept of a decision-support system for responses to tariff-induced uncertainty and disruptions
Source title: Annals of Operations Research
Affiliations: Berlin School of Economics and Law, Department of Business Administration, Berlin, 10825, Germany
Authors with affiliations: Ivanov D., Berlin School of Economics and Law, Department of Business Administration, Berlin, 10825, Germany
Abstract: In this paper, we present a conceptual design for a decision-support system to address tariff-induced uncertainty and disruptions. The system is comprised of predictive (simulation) and prescriptive (optimization) supply chain analytics supplemented by an LLM module for real-time disruption detection. We illustrate applications of the system developed in AnyLogistix supply chain optimization and simulation software and offer generalized mathematical formulations. The experimental part includes several supply chain stress tests under different tariff scenarios, conducted using discrete-event simulation, and recommendations for proactive supply chain reconfiguration via network optimization. This study has both theoretical contributions and practical implications. For the first time, we conceptualize a decision-support system specifically tailored to the specifics of tariff-induced uncertainty. We also show how the decision-support system proposed can be extended toward a digital twin. Our models can be used immediately in practice for stress testing supply chain resilience and for reconfiguration in response to tariff shocks. © The Author(s) 2026.

Abstract: Autonomous vehicles operating near handling limits are vulnerable to sensor and actuator faults. A single biased measurement or a degraded steering actuator can turn a small tracking error into a loss of control. Existing fault-tolerant Model Predictive Control (MPC) methods usually assume perfect fault classification, treat one fault type at a time, or rely on offline digital twins that cannot adapt during a fault episode. This paper proposes a hybrid physics–data digital twin coupled with a robust MPC formulation. The data-driven part is an online Kernel Principal Component Analysis (KPCA) model that updates every 20 control cycles from a rolling window of recent state–input pairs. Fault detection and classification act on the raw measurements, upstream of any state reconstruction, through four mechanism-matched signature tests: a high-pass energy ratio of the speed signal (sensor noise), a latched step in the measured speed (sensor drift), a steering-feedback residual between the applied and commanded angle (actuator fault), and a sustained lateral-error offset (sensor bias). All thresholds are adapted from a 200-step fault-free baseline. Because the drift and actuator tests identify the fault magnitude at detection, the corresponding corrections are applied before the MPC rather than learned afterwards. The classifier separates the four fault classes at 97.2% accuracy (bias 93.2%, drift 100%, actuator 99.2%, noise 94.6%) with a mean cost of 0.7 ms per cycle. A confidence-weighted constraint-tightening scheme maps the real-time twin uncertainty into the size of the MPC tube. The framework is evaluated in simulation on a 1:10 scale autonomous racing platform (mass 1.98 kg, wheelbase 0.25 m, top speed 5 m/s) that follows the Verschueren racing circuit for 15.8 s at Ts = 20 ms under a fixed sequential fault schedule in which the bias and noise faults overlap for 56 cycles. Relative to uncompensated faulty operation the framework cuts lateral root-mean-square error (RMSE) from 0.164 m to 0.031 m (81%) and velocity RMSE from 0.157 m/s to 0.060 m/s (62%), bringing both to within 3% of the fault-free run; a per-window decomposition shows that the residual difference is confined to the 56 noisy speed samples, while the drift window is tracked at the fault-free level because the identified offset is removed before the speed loop sees it. Mean computation time stays below 10 ms per 20 ms control cycle. The paper also discusses what is needed to migrate the framework from the desktop-CPU simulation platform to a production automotive electronic control unit. © 2020 IEEE.

Title: A Digital-Twin-Driven Framework for Traffic and Energy Management Leveraging Generative AI
Source title: 2026 5th MEC International Conference on Advanced Data Analytics and Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Smart Cities, ICADAAI 2026
Affiliations: Indira Gandhi University, Dept. of Cse, Meerpur, Rewari, India; Middle East College, Dept. of Computing and Electronic Engg., Oman

Abstract: With urbanisation, pressures in urban areas and the pressure of climate are increasing, cities may need smart and data-based decision making by implementing intelligent operations and strategic action architectures. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) represents a revolution in smart city management with the potential to generate such data, perform urban analysis and consider policy alternatives, among other things, when there is an uncertainty. Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) are the latest generation of urban analytics such as models for generating scenarios and understanding semantic analysis, with diffusion models and large language models (LLMs). Generative models should not be part of decisions, but instead can be used as one end with UDTs and optimization pipeline and integrated within our city decision-support (CDA) architecture. We propose that the next generation is a general model for such a unified model, based on both the global and a customized algorithm based across cities that combines spatio-temporal and digital twin problem modelling methods and models together and provide multivariable approach in urban decision-making from multiple dimensions. We model the framework in traffic signal control and energy demand response tasks on calibrated synthetic cities' urban data. The spatio-temporal GAN (ST-GAN) and conditional VAE (cVAE) are trained and compared to standard deterministic LSTM and Gaussian process baselines based on both the prediction and quality metrics (RMSE, DTW and coverage) for the performance (expected delay, peak-to-average ratio and worst-case load). We conducted our experiments and showed that GenAI-based decision pipelines significantly outperform traditional baselines for predictive accuracy as well as case diversity and decision robustness in real world smart city data. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: An Environment-Aware Approach for Ultra-Reliable and Low-Latency Communications Under Abrupt Channel Changes
Source title: IEEE Wireless Communications Letters

Abstract: Environmental dynamics around moving users can induce abrupt channel changes, making pilot-based estimation inaccurate and degrading transmission reliability. This letter introduces a Digital Twin (DT)-assisted environment-aware approach that proactively detects such changes and adapts transmission schemes to ensure ultra-reliable and low-latency communications. By accounting for DT modeling uncertainties, we predict a window in which abrupt channel changes are likely to occur and characterize the associated channel dynamics. Building on this prediction, we design a two-layer scheme that integrates fountain coding with optimized pilot and power allocation. Simulation results show that the proposed method achieves ultra-high reliability while maintaining high spectral efficiency under abrupt channel changes. © 2012 IEEE.

Title: Interpreting satellite radar for bridges: integrating MT-InSAR with physics-based and data-driven models for scalable structural health monitoring
Source title: Intelligent Transportation Infrastructure
Affiliations: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, Florida International University, Miami, 33174, FL, United States; Department of Civil Engineering, Kasetsart University, Bangkok, 10900, Thailand
Authors with affiliations: Khan A.Q., Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, Florida International University, Miami, 33174, FL, United States; Pimanmas A., Department of Civil Engineering, Kasetsart University, Bangkok, 10900, Thailand
Abstract: Multi-Temporal Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (MT-InSAR) has matured into a credible, non-contact technique for monitoring bridge deformation from individual structures to regional portfolios. The main challenge for routine engineering use is no longer measuring millimetre-scale line-of-sight (LOS) displacement, but interpreting those measurements into defensible statements about structural condition. This review addresses that interpretation problem by synthesising the physical and algorithmic fundamentals of MT-InSAR, bridge-typology-dependent applicability, LOS projection ambiguity, current sensor capabilities, and emerging open data services. Particular emphasis is placed on signal decoupling because measured bridge displacement combines reversible thermal response, transient live-load effects, progressive deformation associated with damage or settlement, and measurement noise. Two complementary interpretation strategies are examined: physics-based integration using finite-element analysis, model updating and digital twins, and data-driven integration using clustering, anomaly detection, forecasting and deep learning. Their convergence through physics-informed methods is also discussed. The review proposes a hybrid framework in which data-driven methods screen bridge portfolios and identify anomalous deformation, while physics-based modelling provides structural interpretation and supports validation using inspection records, in-situ measurements and uncertainty quantification. The synthesis highlights the strengths and limitations of current practice and identifies research needs in multi-geometry analysis, dense spatial sampling, physics-informed learning, portfolio-scale digital twins and prospective validation. The resulting framework is intended to support scalable, physically interpretable and evidence-based use of MT-InSAR in bridge structural health monitoring. © The Author(s) 2026. Abstract: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) deployments increasingly adopt publish–subscribe middleware to improve scalability, latency, and interoperability across heterogeneous field sites. Data Distribution Service (DDS) is a prominent real-time publish–subscribe standard that provides fine-grained Quality-of-Service (QoS) controls and security extensions, yet its data-centric communication model also introduces distinct attack surfaces, including topic spoofing, unauthorized publishers/subscribers, replay and delay injection, QoS abuse, and control-relevant data poisoning. This paper presents an intrusion detection and prevention system tailored to SCADA-over-DDS, emphasizing uncertainty-aware, autonomous decision-making. We evaluate the framework using replayed industrial control system traces in an emulated industrial testbed designed to approximate DDS-SCADA deployments, and additionally perform cross-dataset generalization experiments and a closed-loop digital twin simulation to assess cyber-physical coupling. No live physical process or operational industrial site was used. The framework formalizes SCADA-over-DDS as a closed-loop cyber-physical system with a middleware-mediated observation channel and proposes a multi-layer architecture that (i) fuses protocol, timing, and control-invariant signals; (ii) quantifies epistemic uncertainty for detection outputs; and (iii) executes prevention actions through a risk-sensitive policy constrained by control-safety envelopes. Under the evaluated conditions, the framework demonstrates detection accuracy (F1 > 0.93), inference latency (<250μs), and tamper-evident logging with measurable advantages including 54% reduction in false alarms and 79% fewer operator notifications over deterministic baselines and centralized database alternatives. © 2014 IEEE.

Title: Noise-robust knowledge distillation for industrial digital twins

Affiliations: Henan University Of Science And Technology, School Of Information Engineering, Luoyang, China; Henan University Of Science And Technology, School Of Software, Luoyang, China
Authors with affiliations: Li Y., Henan University Of Science And Technology, School Of Information Engineering, Luoyang, China; Sun S., Henan University Of Science And Technology, School Of Software, Luoyang, China; Cao Z., Henan University Of Science And Technology, School Of Information Engineering, Luoyang, China
Abstract: Recent advances in Knowledge Distillation (KD) have highlighted the importance of decoupling target and non-target class knowledge. However, in complex scenarios such as industrial digital twins, input data is frequently corrupted by random noise due to electromagnetic interference or sensor aging. While existing fixed-weight distillation strategies perform well on clean data, they exhibit severe vulnerabilities in noisy environments: when the input image is perturbed, the teacher network's predictions for non-target classes contain substantial random fluctuations. Maintaining a high weight for these predictions forces the student network to mimic meaningless noise patterns, leading to significant performance degradation.To overcome this limitation, we propose Adaptive Noise-Aware Knowledge Distillation (ANA-KD), a parameter-free, bidirectional dynamic weight adjustment framework tailored for noisy industrial environments. First, we introduce an information entropy-based noise perception mechanism that quantifies the pollution level of the current sample by measuring the uncertainty in the teacher network's predictive probability distribution. Furthermore, we propose a "scissors-like"bidirectional adaptive weighting strategy. Upon detecting high-noise inputs, the algorithm dynamically reduces the weight β to actively filter out corrupted detailed dark knowledge, while simultaneously increasing the weight α to guide the student network to focus on robust backbone structural features. Extensive experiments across varying noise intensities and network architectures on CIFAR-100 demonstrate the effectiveness of ANA-KD. Particularly under severe noise interference, the proposed algorithm exhibits exceptional defense capabilities without introducing any additional convolutional parameters, ensuring high efficiency for edge deployment. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: Diagnosis and prognosis of the structural health state based on online monitoring data is crucial for enabling condition-based maintenance and ensuring the safety of aeronautical structures. However, most existing studies focus on structural damage diagnosis and prognosis at the individual level, often overlooking the potential of utilizing fleet-wide data, which requires accurately measuring the similarity between structures and the correlation of damage states across individuals in the fleet. To address this, we propose a novel method for fleet-level structural damage diagnosis and prognosis that leverages the similarity of individual structural features. The method introduces a Physics-Decoded Variational Neural Network, enabling accurate extraction of structural features as well as quantifying damage. Additionally, a copula function is used to model the joint probability distribution of damage states across different structures, based on structural feature similarity metrics. This approach allows for collaborative updating of damage states across the fleet using observations from individual structures during the diagnosis process. Validation on a typical damaged aeronautical panel demonstrates that the proposed method achieves more accurate diagnosis and prognosis of individual structural damage states within a fleet, while reducing uncertainties during service compared to conventional individual-based approaches. This method shows promise for integration into a fleet-level airframe digital twin framework, advancing the implementation of condition-based maintenance across fleets. © 2025 Elsevier Masson SAS

Abstract: Digital Twins (DTs) for Water Distribution Networks (WDNs) require accurate state estimation with limited sensors. Uniform sampling often wastes resources across nodes with different uncertainty. We propose an adaptive framework combining LSTM forecasting and Conformal Prediction (CP) to estimate node-wise uncertainty and focus sensing on the most uncertain points. Marginal CP is used for its low computational cost, suitable for real-time DTs. Experiments on Hanoi, Net3, and CTOWN show 33%–34% lower demand error than uniform sampling at 40% coverage and maintain 89.4–90.2% empirical coverage with only 5%–10% extra computation. Abstract: Future 6G wireless networks require communication paradigms that go beyond traditional bit-based transmission toward intelligent, task-oriented information exchange. This paper proposes a Digital Twin-aided semantic communication framework that integrates knowledge-driven semantic inference, end-to-end deep learning-based physical-layer optimization, and cognitive multi-objective optimization. Unlike fully data-driven semantic systems, the proposed semantic transmission is formulated as a statistical inference problem, where task-relevant information is modeled probabilistically and optimized under channel uncertainty. An end-to-end learnable physical layer minimizes reconstruction distortion while maximizing semantic efficiency. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed model reduces mean squared error from 0.185 to 0.132 at 0 dB SNR and 0.072 to 0.038 at 10 dB SNR compared to conventional systems. Semantic accuracy reaches 74.5% at low SNR, 98.6% at high SNR, with a semantic efficiency of 0.87. Furthermore, Digital Twin-assisted cognitive optimization reduces average latency from 42.6 ms to 27.8 ms, energy consumption from 18.9 mJ to 11.3 mJ, and improves adaptability to 0.86. The proposed framework provides an interpretable, scalable, and AI-native foundation for next-generation 6G communication systems. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Financial Performance Outcomes of AI-Adoption in Oil and Gas: The Mediating Role of Operational Efficiency

Authors with affiliations: Mardanov E., BA School of Business and Finance, University of Latvia, Raiņa bulvāris 19, Riga, LV-15865, Latvia; Mavlutova I., BA School of Business and Finance, University of Latvia, Raiņa bulvāris 19, Riga, LV-15865, Latvia; Sloka B., BA School of Business and Finance, University of Latvia, Raiņa bulvāris 19, Riga, LV-15865, Latvia
Abstract: The oil and gas sector operates in a high-risk environment defined by capital intensity, regulatory uncertainty, and volatile commodity prices. Although Artificial Intelligence (AI) is widely promoted as a lever for profitability, the mechanisms through which AI adoption translate into financial outcomes remain insufficiently specified in the oil and gas literature. Grounded in the Resource-Based View and Technology Adoption Theory, this study combines bibliometric mapping of 201 Scopus-indexed publications (2010–2025) with a focused comparative case analysis of important players (BP and Shell), based on publicly reported operational and financial indicators (e.g., operating cost, uptime-related evidence, and return on average capital employed—ROACE). Keyword co-occurrence analysis identifies five thematic clusters showing that efficiency-oriented AI use cases (optimization, automation, predictive maintenance, and digital twins) dominate the research landscape. A thematic synthesis of five highly cited studies further indicates that AI-enabled operational improvements are most consistently linked to measurable cost, productivity, or revenue effects. Case evidence suggests that large-scale predictive maintenance and digital twin programs can support capital efficiency by reducing unplanned downtime and structural costs, contributing to more resilient ROACE trajectories amid price swings. Overall, the findings support a conceptual pathway in which operational efficiency is a primary channel through which AI can create financial value, while underscoring the need for future firm-level empirical mediation tests using standardized KPIs. © 2026 by the authors.

Title: Statistical Validation of Rotor Computational Model

Authors with affiliations: Porto E.H., School of Mechanical Engineering – University of Campinas, Campinas, São Paulo, Brazil; Cavalca K.L., School of Mechanical Engineering – University of Campinas, Campinas, São Paulo, Brazil; Alves D.S., School of Mechanical Engineering – University of Campinas, Campinas, São Paulo, Brazil
Abstract: Rotating elements are present in almost every machine across several applications. Such elements must meet product requirements in order to provide a satisfactory performance without failing, avoiding human and economical losses. Common tools, such as CAE softwares, or even most current tools such as digital twins, should work field-integrated within operating systems to ensure whether products can meet their performance requirements. Verification and Validation assessments are essential for credibility improvements of the machines virtual models that deals with physical quantities, which in turn will be able to perform precise calculations, satisfying the customer demand, assuring reliability and safety, and consequent competitiveness. This work aims to develop and apply a statistical validation – which identifies and takes into account different types of uncertainties in order to assess a software – and contribute to the improvement of the insight proposed in a ASME standard traditional validation. The statistical validation is detailed presented here as well as its advantages and contributions. The developed code analyzes the dynamics of rotating machines through finite element and finite volumes numerical methods for both shaft and hydrodynamic bearings, respectively. Both shaft and hydrodynamic bearing computational models are presented, along with the test rig to be virtually replicated. The obtained results identify the main opportunities of computational model adjustments for motor coupling. The model can be considered as validated in shaft regions far from motor coupling. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

Abstract: This study provides a decision-grade synthesis of floating vertical axis wind turbines (F-VAWTs) for deep-water wind energy, integrating device physics, platform dynamics, farm effects, and bankability over 2012–2025. Standardized searches across Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, ScienceDirect, Taylor & Francis, and SpringerLink returned 237 records; a PRISMA-aligned, motion-aware eligibility cascade and expert adjudication refined this to 123 critical studies. Publication activity rose from one paper in 2012 to a peak of 18 in 2022, then stabilized at 14 in 2023 and 12 per year in 2024–2025, signaling maturation toward fully coupled aero-hydro-servo-elastic modeling. The corpus is dominated by engineering (83) and energy (76) outputs, with growing emphasis on environmental science (42) and mathematics (27), while computer science (5) and earth & planetary sciences (4) remain under-represented—highlighting opportunities for digital twins, physics-informed ML surrogates, and uncertainty-aware control. Geographically, China leads (53 studies), followed by the United Kingdom (20), with Norway and Italy (14 each) forming a robust second tier. Key outlets were Energy and Renewable Energy (∼13 each), Ocean Engineering (12), and Energies (11). Synthesized technical results show that controller-in-the-loop co-design with floater/mooring stiffness can mitigate negative aero-damping and reduce fatigue-critical load spectra; motion-conditioned array layouts (including counter-rotation and staggered spacing) can accelerate wake recovery while easing cable/tendon demands; and validated digital-twin workflows can shorten design loops and enable condition-based O&M. A phase-gated global roadmap is proposed: standards and pilots (2025–2030), 100–300 MW arrays (2031–2040), and autonomous, resilience-oriented fleets (2041–2050), supported by finance and permitting instruments that de-risk motion-coupled offshore assets. © The Author(s) 2026

Title: A Comprehensive Review of Reinforcement Learning Applications in Health Monitoring of Civil Infrastructures

Abstract: The concept of structural health monitoring (SHM) of civil infrastructure has evolved rapidly with the incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI). Although available literature mainly focuses on supervised and unsupervised learning to detect and classify damages, both are inherently limited in addressing sequential decision-making, optimization of long-term maintenance, adaptive sensing, and dynamic uncertainty handling. In comparison, reinforcement learning (RL) offers a policy-based framework that can learn optimal actions by interacting with changing structural and environmental circumstances. Although there is an increasing use of RL applications in SHM, there has not been a comprehensive and critical review of RL applications. This review paper critically evaluates RL approaches used in civil infrastructure SHM, which spans across sensor network optimization, energy management of internet of things (IoT)–based wireless sensor networks (WSNs), updating finite element models (FEMs), contact and noncontact damage detection, unmanned vehicle-based inspection, predictive maintenance planning, autonomous SHM and structural control, etc. The review traces the methodological development from tabular Q-learning to complex deep reinforcement learning (DRL), multiagent systems, hierarchical designs, and combined physics-informed systems. In each of these areas, RL shows a high potential in adaptive resource scheduling, enhanced damage localization, large-scale network maintenance planning, integration of digital twins, federated learning, edge intelligence, and smart infrastructure ecosystems. Nevertheless, a few inherent challenges that prevent large-scale applications, such as high-dimensional state-action spaces, complexity in reward engineering, sample inefficiency, lack of real-world validation, and lack of transferability to heterogeneous infrastructure types, are discussed. Most of the existing implementations are simulation-based or applied to lab-scale models and lack standardized validation procedures for field deployment. Future research should focus on physics-informed and risk-sensitive formulations of RL in safety-critical systems, as well as on scalable multiagent and hierarchical learning designs, transfer and federated learning to alleviate data scarcity and privacy limitations, uncertainty-aware safe exploration strategies, and enhanced interchangeability with IoT-enabled digital twin ecosystems. Through this review, academicians, researchers and industrial experts will get critical insights on RL-based SHM to transform into an intelligent, resilient, sustainable, and autonomous infrastructure monitoring. Authors: Wang J.
Title: The right to uncertainty: strategic indeterminacy and the queering of algorithmic governance
Source title: Third World Quarterly
Affiliations: School of Public Administration, Hubei University, Wuhan, China
Authors with affiliations: Wang J., School of Public Administration, Hubei University, Wuhan, China
Abstract: This research note interrogates the crisis of predictive algorithmic governance in 2026 through the lens of quantum international relations. Integrating the no-cloning theorem with post-colonial and queer theory, it argues that digital twin technologies utilised in contemporary conflict constitute a form of ontological error and necropolitical violence. The paper challenges the Newtonian assumption of the atomistic actor, proposing instead that the global order is an entangled wave function where algorithmic measurement forces a violent ‘collapse’ of political possibility. By engaging with Glissant’s right to opacity and Butler’s ethics of non-violence, it outlines a quantum cosmopraxis, a strategy of strategic indeterminacy designed to resist the epistemic violence of algorithmic coloniality in the Global South. Ultimately, it posits that the refusal to be cloned–or predicted–is the fundamental condition of sovereignty in an entangled world. © 2026 Global South Ltd.

Abstract: Currently, large-scale and high-density industrial robot applications raise non-negligible energy consumption issues. The impact of end-effector payload on energy consumption should not be ignored, as which directly influences the motor torque and energy consumption. This payload often varies unpredictably during the handling of different products or components, leading to uncertain operational conditions. In response, this paper presents a method for optimizing energy efficiency in robotic pick-and-place process under uncertain payload (RPPUP). A digital twin model of the RPPUP system is constructed, which captures and communicates real-time payload data to enable adaptive optimization. A linear-decay proximal policy optimization (LD-PPO) algorithm is employed to dynamically optimize motion efficiency by enabling the robot to learn energy-optimal motion trajectories while adapting to different payloads. LD-PPO introduces a linearly decayed clipping factor, which improves training stability and policy performance in the uncertain payload scenarios. The results verify the feasibility of the proposed method and reduce the 14.40% energy consumption of RPPUP. © 2025 Elsevier Ltd

Abstract: Enabling ultra-reliable, low-latency communication (URLLC) for industrial mobile robots fundamentally relies on accurate, site-specific channel characterization. Stochastic models cannot account for environmental clutter deterministically. Furthermore, current site-specific radio propagation frameworks of network digital twins (NDTs) remain largely unvalidated against continuous 5G measurements in the complex environment of factories. in this paper, we present the design and physical validation of a site-specific radio propagation framework, called FacTwin, for factory NDTs. To achieve high precision, a detailed 3D factory floor model is developed using Blender, incorporating explicit radio frequency (RF) material properties to accurately model wave propagation. NVIDIA Sionna, an open source GPU-accelerated ray-tracing library, is integrated to compute high-resolution radio maps and Reference-Signal-Received-Power (RSRP). For validation, a measurement campaign was conducted in an operational private 5G network in a factory, utilizing an industrial mobile robot to continuously capture RSRP along dynamic paths. A Monte Carlo spatial sampling methodology computationally filters ray-tracing fast-fading artifacts while accounting for robot localization and 3D modeling uncertainties. Compared with ground-truth measurements, FacTwin simulations demonstrate strong spatial alignment, achieving relatively low root mean square error (RMSE) values of 6.78 dB, 5.81 dB, and 7.52 dB across three remote radio units (RRUs). The Monte Carlo spatial sampling improves 90th-percentile accuracy by 3-4 dB and bounds extreme prediction outliers. The results validate the efficacy of FacTwin for site-specific network planning and proactive radio resource management in complex factory environments.  © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: Automated progress monitoring has advanced through reality capture (images, laser scanning, SLAM/mobile mapping) and data-driven interpretation aligned to BIM/4D models. Yet many workflows still stop at percent-complete estimates and leave the schedule-update step under-specified, especially when completion depends on inspections, tests, and formal acceptance. This paper proposes a management-oriented sensing-to-scheduling method that makes that step explicit and computable. First, it separates production-facing progress monitoring from schedule control, highlighting their different units (work vs. time) and decision contexts. Second, it introduces sensor-aware activity scheduling based on evidence: Existence evidence from geometry/vision and performance/acceptance evidence from QA tests, inspections, and approvals. Third, it defines a translation layer that converts measured work quantities into work backlog/forelog, time delay, forecasted finishes, and recovery targets (required productivity) suitable for schedule updating. The approach is designed to complement existing 4D BIM and digital twin pipelines rather than replace them. A small illustrative example demonstrates the calculations and shows how acceptance gates remain explicit milestones. The discussion clarifies applicability, limitations, and research needs for fusing QA data and handling uncertainty. © 2026 International Association on Automation and Robotics in Construction. Title: Desynchronizing the Digital Factory: Relational Intelligence at the Limits of Industrial Artificial Intelligence (AI)
Source title: Science Technology and Human Values
Affiliations: Media, Culture, and Communication, New York University, New York, NY, United States
Authors with affiliations: Kim J.Y., Media, Culture, and Communication, New York University, New York, NY, United States
Abstract: This article examines how industrial artificial intelligence (AI) and digital twin technologies reorganize human labor in a high-tech electric vehicle factory in Vietnam. Corporate narratives portray digitally simulated factories as spaces where human and machine actions can be synchronized and managed through computational intelligence. However, drawing on interviews with welding workers and analysis of industrial AI discourse, I argue that what makes industrial AI work is the human work of “desynchronization.” Workers routinely move beyond digitally prescribed instructions, interpreting machine outputs and adapting to material contingencies that computational models cannot fully anticipate. To explain this process, I develop the concept of relational intelligence: workers’ capacity to coordinate between computational plans and changing workplace realities. Relational intelligence enables workers to complete tasks, accommodate uncertainty, and produce desired outcomes. Industrial AI therefore depends not only on machine intelligence but also on the undervalued human practices that sustain its operation. By foregrounding workers collaborating with industrial AI, who describe themselves as “robots that run on rice,” this article challenges techno-optimistic accounts of automation and digital twins. It argues that the intelligence sustaining industrial AI is not located in machines alone but emerges through workers’ relational intelligence in coordination with computational systems. © The Author(s) 2026

Abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) monitoring in grid-forming (GFM) energy-storage plants exposes multi-rate terminal measurements but rarely the proprietary controller topology, internal states, or gains required by an edge-to-cloud digital twin. We present impedance-conditioned control-structure inversion and sequential parameter identification (ICI-SPI), an IoT-enabled, physics-guided framework that separates structural ambiguity from weak parameter observability. Native-rate waveform tokens are fused with complex dq-impedance evidence; a typed graph decoder then proposes executable controller graphs, which are rejected unless they reproduce both impedance and transient behavior while satisfying structural constraints. A generalized virtual-impedance observer reconstructs hidden electromotive-force states before slow outer-loop and fast inner-loop parameters are fitted in sequence. An observability gate returns a point estimate only when data-Jacobian rank, information, correlation, and uncertainty tests pass; otherwise it reports an interval or a graph-equivalence set. Distillation, integer-8 quantization, and event-triggered synchronization provide an edge-compatible path without conflating local inference cost with communication savings. Controlled electromagnetic-transient (EMT) experiments across virtual-synchronous-machine, droop, matching, and dispatchable-virtual-oscillator controllers yield 96.1% macro-F1, 0.36 typed graph edit distance, and 2.8% impedance normalized root-mean-square error. Selective parameter mean absolute percentage error is 3.2% at 91.3% point-estimate availability. The quantized student retains 95.4% macro-F1 and sends 31% of full digital-twin update packets. These results support structure-first IoT intelligence within the tested controller library and operating envelope. © 2014 IEEE.
